OSCE learning points "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"My case for the prefinal dated on 01\/12\/2023, is a 60 year old woman with chief complaints of shortness of breath and cough since 10 days.\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EE-log link :\u0026nbsp;https:\/\/89aishwaryamuttamsetty.blogspot.com\/2023\/11\/a-75-yo-female-with-sob-and-cough.html\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOSCE learning points :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1) I have learnt the differential diagnosis between bronchial and cardiac asthma.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(Cardiac asthma - wheezing and sudden SOB associated with pink sputum, can never be able to do heavy work as before, associated with rales on auscultation. Occurs mainly due to left heart failure.)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(Bronchial asthma shows only white mucus on coughing, SOB and only acute exacerbations occasionally, with associated wheezing. Occurs due to bronchospasm, inflammation of the airways and excessive mucus production. Easily resolvable.)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) I have learnt how metabolic syndrome, diabetes mellitus and obesity can invariably cause bronchial asthma.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3) I have also learnt the various biomechanisms related to adipokines causing reduced insulin sensitivity in the cells of the body.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4) Learnt to differentiate between rapid, short acting insulin ( clear in appearance), whereas NPH, which is an intermediate acting insulin, is cloudy in appearance (due to presence of buffers like Zinc and protamine)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E5) Learnt the steps of management of asthma :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- beta 2 agonists (levosalbutamol, terbutaline) through metered dose inhaler.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- long acting beta 2 agonists (salmeterol, formeterol), anti cholinergics (Ipratropium bromide) through metered dose inhaler or nebulization.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- corticosteroids administered through nebulization ( budesonide).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Intravenous administration of corticosteroids, which is the first and foremost important step in hospital related management (IV hydrocortisone or prednisolone).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E6) I've also learnt the importance of following up the patient's diet plan post treatment, such as monitoring to make sure her diet has half a plate of fresh fruits and vegetables to combat obesity and associated insulin resistance.\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/89aishwaryamuttamsetty.blogspot.com\/feeds\/8374493509044576672\/comments\/default","title":"Post 60 y\/o female with SOB and cough"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EThis is an a online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient\/ attender was informed the purpose of the information being acquired. An informed consent was taken from patient\/ attender and there is omission of information that was requested to be omitted.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINTS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 60 year old woman came to the OPD with chief complaints of\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- shortness of breath since 10 days.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Dry cough since 10 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 10 days ago, when she developed shortness of breath grade 2 mMRC, that was insidious in onset, gradually progressive, aggravated on exposure to cold and dust.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/O of orthopnea, wheeze\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDry cough is also present since 7 days, no aggravating or relieving factors present.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O fever, chest pain, chest tightness, hemoptysis, sweating, palpitations\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O weight loss\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPAST HISTORY\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESimilar complaints 10 years ago. Usage of rotahaler (Fluticasone + vilantrol)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient on Tab. Acebrophyllin 100mg PO\/BD.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient on Diabetic medication.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O TB, epilepsy, thyroid disorders, HTN, CAD in the past.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFAMILY HISTORY\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot significant\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiet - Mixed\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAppetite - Normal\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESleep- Adequate\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBowel and bladder movements- Normal\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAddictions - None\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo known allergies seen.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETREATMENT HISTORY\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EStopped diabetic medication since 5 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EInhaler usage since 10 years for asthma.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O blood transfusions or surgeries.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGENERAL PHYSICAL EXAMINATION\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient is conscious, coherent and cooperative.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWith moderate built and nourishment.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPallor - no\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIcterus - no\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECyanosis - no\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EClubbing - no\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EKoilonychia - no\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELymphadenopathy -
